score.meaning: Strong, coherent and personally grounded local signature implementation with a clear owner-selected lead. The remaining shortfall is primarily the small-screen signature gesture and the degree of distinctive authorship conveyed by the current static application; this is not a claim of measured recognition or a numerical motion-quality judgment.

strengths: Investigate & share turns the previous broad emotion catalogue into a chosen recurring behavior. Nag explicitly prefers its warmth and curiosity; that resolves owner fit within its stated scope.

The character now attends to one actual project question and returns toward the visitor. The eva.md link and exploratory Markdown/Git description avoid inventing success, failure, adoption or biography.

The desktop image puts heyNag, a named project and the character in one readable composition. The README adds first-person work evidence, while the signature page retains Nag and Nagarjuna Boddu attribution.
The unequal paddle antennae, soft large head, four marked wings, compact body and stub feet remain visibly coherent in the paint and pose sheets. Palette changes do not create a second character.

The selected paint change is modest and preserves the face-first hierarchy. Keeping a paper-ground day avatar for universal small account use is more defensible than claiming equivalent night-stem readability at 32px.

The page starts at a canonical still, offers deliberate finite playback and leaves the question/link available independently of motion. Source pauses on hiding/offscreen, and reduced motion retains a pose. This supports repeat visits without making attention-seeking behavior the identity.
The wry and one-peek treatments remain supporting studies. They add optional personality without overriding Nag's chosen warm lead or changing tiny anatomy.

deductions.claim: The presenting mitten contributes too little to the signature at 390px.
deductions.basis: signature-390.png shows an approximately 105px-wide visible moth in a narrow side-by-side column. Glasses and antennae remain readable, but the open mitten merges perceptually with ruff/chest detail; sizes-refined.png shows the same density at small full-figure scales.
deductions.implication: The copy carries 'share' more strongly than the character at this width. This is not evidence that humans fail to understand it, and it is not a reason to enlarge hands or replace the anatomy.
deductions.action: For future phone staging, compare a wider character region or a deliberately restaged composition. Preserve the screen-right question eye-line; merely stacking the current cue below would contradict the authored gaze.

deductions.claim: The static signature is more strongly 'friendly curious person' than a highly specific Nag behavior.
deductions.basis: The canonical invitation uses glasses, a soft smile and a tiny raised hand; the real project cue provides the strongest particular association. 'One question leads to another' and 'Notice something. Look a little closer. Bring someone along' are coherent but broadly reusable language.
deductions.implication: This is a strong foundation, not yet a fully ownable behavioral shorthand. It does not mean the approved warm lead should become more mischievous, loud or anatomically elaborate.
deductions.action: Carry the same small repertoire into a second verified project moment with one actual detail or decision from Nag's work, using first-person authorship. Repetition with truthful specific content can establish distinctiveness without adding decorative movement.

deductions.confidence: high for image evidence; low for audience outcome
deductions.claim: The head-only avatar trades the most obvious moth cue for face readability.
deductions.basis: sizes-refined.png shows a coherent 32–64px paper-ground face/antenna mark, but the four marked wings are outside that crop; night 32px stems are weaker still.
deductions.implication: The avatar's recognition burden rests on head contour and unequal paddles. Keep that scope explicit rather than presenting every crop as equally distinctive.
deductions.action: Retain day paper-ground universal avatar and introduce it near heyNag/full figure when feasible. Later compare unaided attribution and delayed recall; do not redesign from an untested confusion hypothesis.

improvementCriteria: Preserve tiny anatomy, theme geometry parity, the owner-selected warm lead, the full project question and immediate access to real work.

Demonstrate that the finite signature's look-to-question and return-to-visitor survive its smallest intended application, with a phone layout that gives the mitten enough space or honestly assigns the meaning to static copy.

Establish a small repeated signature repertoire across truthful project-specific moments, with Nag's first-person contribution visible; avoid making the full 24-emotion catalogue the default brand behavior.
Review the actual revised exports and a final source manifest before extending this assessment to those files.

Keep expert appeal, owner fit, native-device usability, unprimed emotion comprehension, Nag attribution and delayed recall as separate evidence categories. Audience testing would support broader claims, not automatically raise this craft score.

confidence.overall: medium-high for local brand system and inspected stills
confidence.sourceBehavior: medium: read code and root evidence, did not operate UI

implementedAssessment: The agreed signature-selection experiment is materially implemented rather than merely proposed: three studies exist separately from 24 emotions, the selected study is the default, the real eva.md cue stays stable, and still/reduced-motion use is designed. The original concern that the emotional library lacked a selected brand behavior is substantially resolved. Support acceptance of this local study with named small-screen and evidence limits; do not call it a completed website or validated recognizable identity.

workflowChanges: Begin each future website brief with the actual Nag project question, verified public evidence, intended reader action, and one chosen signature behavior. Brand determines meaning before engineering chooses timing.
Review the 50th visit as well as the first: static useful content, one opt-in finite performance, no hover/idle motion added by default. Record why every moving element earns attention.

Before implementation, cast real project content as informational lead, character as expressive support, optional ornaments as static; write cause-to-response beats and keep the destination usable throughout.

Produce matched desktop and smallest intended-size frames, then separate continuous live playback and native-phone evidence. Tag each conclusion by its evidence source rather than collapsing them into 'tested'.

Use full relevant skill instructions in the responsible engineering/review role, preserve independent paired reviews, and discuss applicable exceptions. Brand accepts the meaningful behavior, not a generic under-300ms rule.
Keep a single truthfully attributed project cue through a performance; use source version hashes and fresh exports to prevent an older successful capture from approving a newer uninspected source.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason: Generic UI duration/stagger budgets do not compress a 4.1-second opt-in character thought into 300ms. The content and controls remain immediately usable; acting order carries meaning.

'Never animate keyboard actions' removes incidental control animation, not an explicitly requested Play action that a keyboard user should also be able to invoke; reduced-motion preference still governs movement.
'Only transform and opacity' is not permission to delete tiny mittens, wing markings or antenna geometry. Any engine optimization requires measured bottlenecks and preserved character invariants.
Attention-loop examples are not a recommendation to add idle loops: the selected finite still-first behavior already serves repeat visits.
Mobile-native's blanket app-shell baseline is conditional. This is a scrolling document; it does not justify disabling native document scrolling, pinch zoom or text selection.

Skills' implementation output instructions do not authorize this reviewer to edit source; root explicitly owns implementation/browser work. I use their review principles and record scoped observations.
Swift/Expo, Sonner, drag/sheet recipes and library selection have no current implementation target. Explicit-only prototype/pick-ui-library are not silently invoked by catalog inspection.
